SQLite is an embedded database that lives in a single file inside your app process, so there is no server to install, configure or back up beyond copying the file. For a small web app with modest traffic it is often the simplest choice.

PostgreSQL is a full client-server database with strong concurrency, rich types and extensions. It needs a server to run, but it handles many simultaneous writers and scales well as the product grows.
